Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

culture noun

a people’s way of life: its customs, beliefs and arts

also cultures, cultural, civilization, civilisation, way of life

classical

Nep. Paus. 3.1: nōn enim mōrēs patriōs sōlum, sed etiam cultum vestītumque mūtāvit
M-O s.v. civilized: culture: mōrēs

mōrēs, mōrum m. pl.

noun, third declension, plural

a people’s ways: its customs and way of life

With īnstitūta and lēgēs, what we call a people’s culture. For one custom see practice (custom).

Other words

  • cultus, cultūs m. — a way of life, civilisation: how a people lives, dresses and eats

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.1.3: ā cultū atque hūmānitāte prōvinciae longissimē absunt; Cic. de Or. 1.33: ā ferā agrestīque vītā ad hunc hūmānum cultum cīvīlemque dēdūcere

    Lewis & Short: care directed to the refinement of life, that is style, manner of life, culture, civilisation. Morgan–Owens: cultus cīvīlis, cultus hūmānus.

  • īnstitūta, īnstitūtōrum n. pl. — a people’s institutions and customs

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.1.2: hī omnēs linguā, īnstitūtīs, lēgibus inter sē differunt

    For one established practice see practice (custom).

  • hūmānitās, hūmānitātis f. — civilisation, as against barbarism

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.1.3; Tac. Agr. 21.3: idque apud inperītōs hūmānitās vocābātur

    Tacitus, of the Britons taking to porticoes, baths and dinner parties: the naive called it civilisation, when it was part of their slavery.

  • cultūra, cultūrae f. — cultivation, farming

    noun, first declension · avoid · classical · Cic. Off. 1.151: nihil est agrī cultūrā melius

    Not a people’s culture: classically the tilling of land, and by metaphor the cultivation of the mind (see culture, learning and the arts).

Examples

  • Hī omnēs linguā, īnstitūtīs, lēgibus inter sē differunt.

    They all differ from one another in language, customs and laws.Caes. BG 1.1.2

  • Nōn enim mōrēs patriōs sōlum, sed etiam cultum vestītumque mūtāvit.

    For he changed not only the ways of his own country but his whole way of life and his dress as well.Nep. Paus. 3.1

See also practice, culture, language, national, foreign.
